title: quadlet: generated ExecStart flag order is non-deterministic (string keys iterated from a Go map)
body:
### Issue Description

Quadlet emits the podman flags for several `[Container]` keys (`ShmSize`, `StopTimeout`, `Memory`, `PidsLimit`, ...) in a random order. The same `.container` file yields a different `ExecStart=` line on each generator run, i.e. on every `systemctl daemon-reload`.

Cause: `lookupAndAddString()` and `lookupAndAddAllStrings()` in `pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go` range over a `map[string]string` (`stringKeys` in `ConvertContainer()`, also the pod/kube/network key maps), and Go randomises map iteration order:

```go
func lookupAndAddString(unit *parser.UnitFile, group string, keys map[string]string, podman *PodmanCmdline) {
        for key, flag := range keys {
                if val, ok := unit.Lookup(group, key); ok && len(val) > 0 {
                        podman.add(flag, val)
                }
        }
}
```

Present in v5.8.8 and on `main` as of today.

Semantics are unaffected, but the generated unit's content changes without any input change. That breaks anything that hashes or diffs generated units to detect configuration drift (config management, audit tooling): our automation restarted containers on every run because the unit's checksum kept changing.

#28172 is the same class of bug in a different code path (`kube play` networks).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a unit in an empty directory:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/qrepro
   cat > /tmp/qrepro/repro.container <<'EOF'
   [Container]
   Image=docker.io/library/alpine:latest
   ShmSize=64m
   StopTimeout=10
   Memory=128m
   PidsLimit=100
   EOF
   ```

2. Run the generator several times and compare `ExecStart`:

   ```sh
   for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
     QUADLET_UNIT_DIRS=/tmp/qrepro \
       /usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator --dryrun 2>/dev/null \
       | grep '^ExecStart=' | sha256sum
   done | sort | uniq -c
   ```


### Describe the results you received

8 runs, 6 distinct `ExecStart` lines. Two consecutive runs:

```
ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run --name systemd-%N --replace --rm --cgroups=split --pids-limit 100 --shm-size 64m --memory 128m --stop-timeout 10 --sdnotify=conmon -d docker.io/library/alpine:latest
ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run --name systemd-%N --replace --rm --cgroups=split --stop-timeout 10 --memory 128m --pids-limit 100 --shm-size 64m --sdnotify=conmon -d docker.io/library/alpine:latest
```

### Describe the results you expected

Identical output for identical input: iterate the keys in a fixed order (e.g. sorted keys, or an ordered slice of key/flag pairs instead of a map).

### podman info output

```
podman version 5.8.8 (Debian package 5.8.8, amd64)
OS: Debian 12 (bookworm) based
rootful, system generator (/run/containers/systemd)
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Reproduced in a QEMU VM; the generator code path is environment-independent (Go map iteration order).

### Additional information

Happens on every run; no special setup beyond two or more of the affected keys in one unit.

**AI disclosure:** this bug was found, diagnosed and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic, model `claude-opus-5-5`), running in Claude Code during a test run of our infrastructure automation in a VM. Specifically, Claude:

- noticed containers restarting with no configuration change and traced it to the generated unit's checksum changing between daemon-reload`s,
- located the cause in `quadlet.go` (map iteration in `lookupAndAddString`/`lookupAndAddAllStrings`, v5.8.8 and `main`),
- wrote and ran the reproduction above (8 dry runs, 6 distinct outputs) and searched for existing issues,
- drafted this report.

A human (the reporter) reviewed it and filed it.

comments.body:
The output format is not meant to be stable. Any config checks should be done on the source quadlet file but never the output IMO.

cc @ygalblum

@Luap99 is correct, the output is not meant to be deterministic. Furthermore, part of the reason we implemented Quadlet was to be able to make changes/fixes to the output based on changes in Podman without having to change the Quadlet file. The Quadlet files are the source of truth for configuration changes, not the output

Thanks both - that makes sense. Treating the quadlet file as the source of truth, and the generated unit as an implementation detail that may change between Podman versions, is a reasonable design.
                                                                                      
We've already moved our drift detection to hash the quadlet source instead of the generated unit, so the non-deterministic order no longer affects us. Closing.
